content: Global credit markets are on edge as fresh loan blowups fuel credit risk concerns and stir memories of the 2023 US regional banking crisis. US high-yield and leveraged-loan funds each had $1.3 billion of outflows in the latest week, the most in six months, according to LSEG Lipper, a sign that investors are readjusting their holdings of higher-risk debt. Meghan Graper, global head of debt capital markets at Barclays, speaks with Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield".  (Source: Bloomberg)
